name: Fantasy in four parts
hint: Home, the wide world, the darkness and the return, with magic that exacts its price all the way. Works for both epic and urban fantasy.

parts.title: Home
chapters: An ordinary day with a crack
The main character in action in a concrete everyday life, and a first sign that something is wrong. Ground the reader before you explain.
The call
Something pulls them out of everyday life, and it ties into the book's big what if. They hesitate, and the reader understands why.
The first magic
The reader sees magic up close and sees what it costs, so the rules are set in action rather than in a lecture.
The departure
They choose to leave, or are forced to, and the door home closes behind them. In urban fantasy, this is the step into the hidden world.

parts.title: The wide world
chapters: New ground
A new realm, a new people or the city's hidden side brings wonder, but also customs and rules the main character breaks.
Companions and enemies
Alliances form between people with goals of their own, which chafe against the main character's.
The trial
They try to solve something with magic or skill and fail, or pay too much. The limits become clear.
The midpoint
A truth about the world, the magic or the enemy turns the quest, and they stop reacting and start acting.

parts.title: The darkness
chapters: The enemy strikes
The antagonist's plan turns out larger than anyone believed, and what has been won so far is lost.
The price is paid
Someone or something pays the full cost of magic: a companion, a memory, a part of the main character.
The darkest hour
All seems lost, and they see what they have given up along the way.
The insight
The answer lies in something the reader already knows: a rule, a cost or a promise from earlier in the book.

parts.title: The return
chapters: The final battle
The conflict is decided in battle, by cunning or through a sacrifice, but always by rules the reader already knows and by the main character's own choice. No new powers at the last minute.
What has changed
What victory cost, and how both the world and the main character have changed. Home is not what it was.
